page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 56 virtual CPUs mapped to 28 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 224.0 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This configuration does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, meaning all storage requirements must be fulfilled via network-attached block storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Memory performance is a notable highlight; the PassMark memory score ranks in the top 10%, supported by a cached small-block read memory bandwidth of 3877.36 GB/sec. However, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidths drop to average levels at 137.27 GB/sec and 68.92 GB/sec respectively. Computational tasks such as software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing demonstrate strong performance, while single-core operations and text processing remain in the average tier.

With its high core density and strong multi-threaded performance, this instance is suited for compute-heavy workloads such as compilation pipelines, database operations, and medium-scale LLM text generation. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a balanced resource profile for general-purpose enterprise applications that require dedicated CPU allocation without the overhead of GPU acceleration. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of physical AMD EPYC cores and top-tier memory performance, though the lack of bundled local storage requires external storage provisioning which should be factored into overall infrastructure design.
